n.description: Number of nodes (customers) in the network

p.description: Number of nodes to be selected as medians

c.description: Service cost between every ordered pair of nodes; c_{ij} is the cost of serving node i from median j

assumptions.description: The number of medians to open is at least one and strictly less than the number of nodes.
The cost from any node to itself is zero.

code.python: assert all(c[i][i] == 0 for i in range(n))

assumptions.description: The cost between any two distinct nodes is strictly positive.
assumptions.formulation: c_{ij} > 0 \quad \forall i, j \in \{0, \ldots, n-1\},\ i \neq j

code.python: assert all(c[i][j] > 0 for i in range(n) for j in range(n) if i != j)

x.description: x_{ij} is 1 if node i is served by median j, 0 otherwise; the diagonal entry x_{jj} is 1 iff node j is selected as a median

constraints.description: Every node is served by exactly one median.
A node may be served by another node only if that node is selected as a median.
constraints.formulation: x_{ij} \leq x_{jj} \quad \forall i, j \in \{0, \ldots, n-1\},\ i \neq j

constraints.description: Exactly p nodes are selected as medians.

code.gurobipy: model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(x[j, j] for j in range(n)) == p)

objective.description: Minimize the total service cost summed over all nodes.

code.gurobipy:
model.setObjective(
    gp.quicksum(c[i][j] * x[i, j] for i in range(n) for j in range(n)),
    GRB.MINIMIZE,
)

notes: This is the classical formulation (CF) of the p-median problem, stated in Section 2 of garcia2011 over a single matrix x whose diagonal entry x_{jj} is the location variable (x_{jj} = 1 iff node j is a median) and whose off-diagonal entries x_{ij} (i != j) are the allocation variables.

The source declares only the location variables x_{jj} as binary and relaxes the allocation variables x_{ij} (i != j) to continuous with x_{ij} >= 0. Here the entire matrix x is binary; this is an equivalent MILP, since the paper notes there is always an optimal solution in which each node is assigned fully to a cheapest open median, so integrality of the allocation variables is free.
The problem-level parametrization (n, p, c) is used directly, so gen_params.py is a pass-through.
